_doc: Factory rules for the canvas Rewards node Coverage Badge + compile-time block dialog. A rule fires per-phase when its `when` clause matches the phase's reward-term breakdown. Critical rules block training when [Canvas] reward_coverage_mode = strict. Counts split into phase-specific (declared via applies_to) and unconditional (applies_to == []), with `all_*` counts being the union (= what actually applies to the phase at runtime). Default policy: a phase is OK as soon as it has at least one positive AND at least one negative term across the union — that matches the runtime mask semantics (unconditional terms apply to every phase). Critical fires only on the Go2 limb-flailing pattern: a 'negative-required' phase (= static) where there is no negative anywhere AND there are unconditional positives that will be exploited. User overlay lives at ~/UnitPort/registers/reward_coverage_rules_custom.json. See registers.rewards_coverage._rule_matches for the supported when fields.

rules.message: Phase has no negative reward at all — neither phase-specific nor unconditional. The policy is free to do anything when this phase is active; expect idle limb-flailing or pose drift.

Phase has no phase-specific negative reward, yet unconditional positive rewards (e.g. feet_air_time / gait) are active in this phase. Without isolation, the policy will exploit those positives in this phase even though they're inappropriate (the static Go2 limb-flailing bug). Add a phase-specific negative term, or scope the unconditional positives via applies_to.
Phase has no positive reward — the policy has no shaping signal toward the desired behavior in this phase.
Phase has zero reward contributions of any kind — completely unsupervised.
